content_title: What will you learn?
content_details:
• You will learn to perform an all-round risk assessment for the intellectual property developed by an organisation and used by it;
  • You will learn how to advise a company on its intellectual property strategy including selection, registration, monetising and protection.
  • You will learn how to draft various applications, specifications and claims related to the registration of intellectual property (copyrights, trademarks and patents) across multiple jurisdictions;
  • You will learn how to draft responses to objections or examination reports from the patents or trademarks registry/offices at the stage of registration for India and the US;
  • You will learn how to draft notices such as a cease and desist notice and also draft responses to such notices;
  • You will learn to draft requisition lists and reports for due diligence of intellectual property conducted at the time of an acquisition or other transaction;
  • You will also learn how to draft various appeals and petitions before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

content_title: Specific Learning Objectives
content_details:
• Learn how to identify what risks an organisation has to its own intellectual property as well as to others’ intellectual property that it uses;
  • Learn about the copyright life cycle and how to deal with works entering the public domain;
  • Learn what online piracy or digital piracy is, how it is connected with intellectual property and the relevant legislation in India and the US;
  • Learn how copyrights work in sporting events, their broadcast and distribution rights;
  • Learn how to deal with copyright disputes before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board;
  • Learn how to use John Doe orders or how criminal prosecution works in order to  enforce copyrights; 
  • Learn how companies select trademarks and why a trademark strategy is required;
  • Learn what non-conventional trademarks are and how these are treated in the US and the EU; 
  • Learn how to secure registration for non-conventional trademarks in India as well as a process before the USPTO and EPO;
  • Learn about international treaties related to trademarks and how these impact the processes in the US and EU
  • Learn how to draft a cease and desist notice, a notice of opposition and a response to a notice of opposition;
  • Learn how to draft and file review and rectification petitions before the Trademarks registry;
  • Learn when and how a cancellation petition can be filed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board;
  • Learn how to draft and file an appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board (IPAB) for copyright as well as trademark matters;
  • Learn what is and is not patentable and how to advise a client on whether or not to proceed with the filing of a patent claim;
  • Learn how to patent specifications and claims can be drafted for specific types of inventions such as pharmaceutical and technological inventions, the challenges that can be faced and how to overcome these challenges;
  • Learn how the examination process works in respect of patents and how to reply to a patents examination report;
  • Learn about how the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board works;
  • Learn about how the patent prosecution process works with the USPTO and various grounds of pre and post-grant opposition;
  • Learn what is patent docketing and how it is used;
  • Learn how to deal with patent-related matters before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, the orders it can pass and the remedies available;
  • Learn about what patent portfolio management is and how large companies manage their patent portfolios;
  • Learning how the patent infringement litigation works in the case of research institutes and what is different about such litigation;
  • Learn about standard-essential patents and how to take care in licensing these;
  • Learn about patent disputes and litigation, as well as cross border patent litigation
  • Learn how to conduct due diligence with respect to the intellectual property of an organisation during an acquisition or other transaction.

content_title: International Arbitration Work and Demand for Young Lawyers Will Increase
content_details:
• A high-volume of technology contracts with foreign parties contain arbitration clauses. These contracts range from INR 50 lakhs to a few crores and are much more in number than construction or infrastructure contracts. The number of disputes arising from these contracts is significant. Owing to the amounts in dispute, opportunities to work in this area are lucrative for arbitration lawyers. 
  • Cash flow issues, recession and market disruption by COVID-19 has increased the number of payment defaults, requiring a combination of mediation and arbitration-related strategies to resolve such disputes.   
  • Clients frequently require their lawyers to give advice on how to draft arbitration clauses in different types of commercial contracts. Specialized arbitration knowledge is important for these contracts to include workable dispute resolution mechanisms. If such contracts are executed without due attention to their arbitration clauses, lawyers may find the trust of clients to be eroded in the time of a dispute.
  • Prices that lawyers can justifiably charge increase with the complexity of the problem that they are solving for clients. International commercial arbitration work is complex, thus making the work lucrative for lawyers who can provide effective results. Amounts in dispute are also of sufficient value. Thus, clients are willing to pay lawyers a good premium for their services.  
  • Clients need lawyers to actively lead the dispute resolution strategy, even if they are not qualified in a foreign jurisdiction. Therefore, ignorance of the law of foreign jurisdictions or lack of a license to practice abroad is not an acceptable reason to be passive. 
  • Internationally, there is development around third party funding of international arbitrations. Countries such as Hongkong, Singapore and France have created an environment to permit such funding.

content_title: Challenges Faced by Lawyers During Performance of Arbitration Work
content_details:
• Transactional lawyers draft arbitration clauses every day, but often make mistakes regarding the aspects of the dispute, leading to unworkable or defective arbitration clauses. The seat vs. venue debate in Indian jurisprudence is an outcome of ‘pathological’ arbitration clauses.
  • Contracts in technology and other sectors are increasing of a cross-border nature - transactional lawyers struggle to provide inputs to clients on which systems of law to choose and why. 
  • With respect to their contracts with foreign parties, clients often want to know - how is the choice of Singapore contract law different from UK contract law, or from Indian contract law? They want their lawyers to compare systems of law like different versions of a software product, or like different laptops or mobile phones. This requires lawyers to possess deep clarity of different legal systems. Due to the territorial nature of legal systems, lawyers have not developed that sense and lack such clarity. 
  • Disputes lawyers step into the picture ‘after the fact’, that is after the damage has been done. They are mostly aware of arbitrations or their enforcement anywhere else other than their home jurisdiction. However, they are frequently required to liaise and collaborate with international counsel with offshore legs of arbitration proceedings, which requires a great deal of familiarity with offshore legal systems and arbitration processes.
  • International commercial arbitration textbooks often focus on the ‘flavours’ and ‘range of possibilities across multiple legal systems. There is inadequate focus on the rules of specific arbitral institutions, specific legal outcomes for a target audience (e.g. in Indian tech companies), and on jurisdictions where there is a high-volume of arbitration from a practitioners’ perspective. Additional independent study and exposure to real arbitrations are required to develop that perspective.

content_title: Difference between international commercial arbitration textbooks, moot court competitions and real-world work
content_details:
• International commercial arbitration textbooks are not jurisdiction-specific and primarily focus on the principles. Application of the principles in each jurisdiction and scenario needs to be learnt by practice. Similarly, textbooks in India primarily focus on Supreme Court judgments. There is a lot of room left for learning the strategy disputes, drafting skills for different documents, rules of different arbitral institutions, enforcement strategies with respect to offshore jurisdictions, etc.  
  • Moot court competitions such as the Willem C. Vis Vienna or Hong Kong are based on conventions such as the CISG, which India is not a signatory to.

  • A technical subject with numerous tricky concepts.

One stop solution to all the above dilemmas is to understand the tricky concepts in detail with the help of illustrations and case laws as well as practice questions at the same time to ensure that the concept becomes clear and concrete in one's mind.
 
Let’s consider the doubts and myths one has when he/she makes up their mind to attain clarity over  Indian Contract Act, 1872:

  • The Indian Contract Act is a compact and unchallenging subject. 
  • It only revolves around illustrations rather than conceptual notions.
  • Only Sections till Section 25 are relevant, rest of the Sections can be left. 
  • There is no logical way to learn and understand the Indian Contract Act
  • A theoretical understanding of the Indian Contract Act seldom has a role to play in practical applicability.

content_title: WHY IS LAWSIKHO LAUNCHING THIS AS A SEPARATE CRASH COURSE?
content_details:
Indian Contract Act has been observed as a major setback in any kind of exam and also when it comes to the practical application of laws, it has been seen to be one of the most functional streams.  

Good things come in small packages, same is the case with Indian Contract Act. The act comes with quite a few diverse and detailed concepts which are essential to be dealt with, while understanding not just the concepts of contracts, but also gaining a grip over other inter-related laws. For example, the concepts of agency and bailment which form paramount parts of the Act cannot be understood without getting to the bottom of fundamental concepts like essentials of formation of a valid contract, how an agreement is formed, when an offer and acceptance is communicated etc..

To get a grasp of each of these concepts, it becomes essential to have a clear idea of the bare act provisions as well as relevant and landmark case laws with interactive and lucid content.
 
A student might feel confident about the concepts of Indian Contract Act, but it's niti-grities make it delusional and deceptive when it comes to actually solving a question based on Indian Contract Act as it has such detailing which can make a person bewilder and can land him in the state of a puzzle because lack of a general expertise over the subject and the manner in which it is taught in most Law Schools and various other institutions is unfortunately not up to the mark for a student to feel confident in attaining clarity. Let us consider an example, A proposes, by letter, to sell something to B at a certain price. B accepts A’s proposal by a letter sent by post. When does the communication of the acceptance is complete as against B (acceptor)? It is not completed when the letter is posted but only when the letter is received by A (offeror). This is how the concepts become tricky and confusing, which should be understood with the help of relevant illustrations to gain clarity.
 
Explore a teaching methodology that has made the subject interesting, interactive and completely antithetical to the idea of rote memorization. How does this help? Well it is a means to achieving an end- the end here being thoroughness of the concepts pertaining to the Indian Contract Act

content_title: Are you attempting the SEBI Grade A Exam (for Legal Manager Position) this year?
content_details:
The SEBI Grade A Officers Position is a highly coveted job, with starting salaries INR 75,000 per month (with accommodation) or INR 1,07,000 per month (without accommodation) and a stable career path. 

There is one caveat. 

The exam is highly competitive. 

Only 34 seats are available, of which 12 seats are for OBC, 8 for SC/ ST and 2 for EWB. Only a fraction of these seats (12) will be for lawyers. (For the Legal stream). [Please note that Lawyers are also eligible to appear for the General Stream]
 
Even the most conservative estimates assume around 20,000 applicants to be sitting for this exam. 

In other words [20,000 minus selected people] will be rejected.

This reflects a pass percentage of 0.2 percent at the maximum.

If you are preparing for the exam, chances are that you don’t want to be one of them.

content_title: Top reasons why young lawyers fail to crack competitive exams
content_details:
• No way to track progress on a day-to-day, month-to-month basis.
  • Preparing for a competitive exam in the same way as a college exam because the syllabus overlaps.
  • Not identifying where they stand in comparison to others.
  • Not creating a sufficiently advanced preparation strategy for a national competitive exam.
  • Absence of consistent guidance.
  • Falling off their strategy.
  • Getting demotivated.
  • Insufficient practice on the exam format.
  • Believing that reading a book is sufficient to prepare for the exam.
  • Confused approach towards answering questions with knowledge gained by reading books.
  • Not measuring retention.
  • Not having a last-minute preparation strategy to revise.

content_title: Do you know the secrets that differentiate the few people who crack the exam from the thousands who don’t?
content_details:
• Measurement of where they stand
  • Guidance of experts
  • Continuous Optimisation of their strategy
  • Fixed path towards revision 
  • Attempts and Re-Attempts in practice until one gains perfection

content_title: It all starts with measurement.
content_details: Peter Drucker, the management guru has said, “You can only improve what you measure.”

content_title: Let us explain the steps that follow afterward.
content_details:
Here is a quick 5-step method: 

  • Perform mock tests to diagnose where you stand, identify your strengths and weaknesses.
  • Get on a coaching call with an expert who can help you identify a strategy to improve.
  • Prepare based on the study plan provided by the coach.
  • Attempt mock tests to track progress.
  • Repeat the method and feel satisfied about progress.

content_title: How can you measure where you stand today, use it to improve your preparation, measure your progress, prepare again?
content_details:
• Measure topic-wise progress, till you master the subject
  • Measure subject-wise progress, till you master all the subjects
  • Measure syllabus-wise progress till you master time management strategy.
  • Measure overall-progress till you master the nuances of the entire syllabus.

We are introducing a set of 6 holistic mock-tests (for Paper-1 and Paper-2 each) to help you practice. content_title: Launching LawSikho Virtual Library for Law Students
content_details:
There has been a long-standing demand for launching a course library that is meant for law students specifically.

Finally, we have been able to do this. Just like there is Master Access available to established lawyers, we are making a special course library available to law students.

We offer dozens of courses to law students depending on the career that they wish to pursue. However, how can they decide early in their career what exactly they would do? Ambitions and interests can rapidly change. Also, some of them, wisely, seek exposure to a larger variety of legal disciplines at this stage of their development.

Apart from that, they also seek 360-degree guidance for their career - whether they want to land the right internships, work at a tier 1 law firm, get the top 1% opportunities in litigation or become a judge for that matter. 

It is for these students that we launched the Students Virtual Career Development Library.

It is for those law students who want to pursue the entire gamut of courses available with LawSikho, including test prep courses and have no limits on their learning opportunities and access.

It can be expensive and hard to pursue multiple courses, one after another, especially when it comes to extensive test prep courses. But the Virtual Career Development Library makes it very affordable and accessible for every law student.

What is included in the Virtual Career Development Library?

In the Virtual Career Development Library, every student will get access to an ever-growing body of legal courses, study material, practice assignments, video tutorials and specialised online live tutoring and guest lectures by top industry experts that can engage your mind and intellect and capture your interests. The library promises to produce massive returns for your budding legal career in terms of enhanced knowledge and skills, higher performance in internships and job interviews, unparalleled student satisfaction and round the year access to one-on-one personalised coaching and guidance.

If you want hard copy material for any of the courses, you can just pay the printing and courier cost, and we will send it to you! We will not make any profit on selling you hard copy material, ever. That’s a promise. However, the price does not include the price of any hard copies.

The Virtual Career Development Library will equip law students to pursue a variety of careers, which are listed below.

Government Job Related Competitive Exams

  • State Judiciary exams
  • SEBI Grade- A Law Officers exam
  • UGC-NET
  • CLAT LLM

 

Litigation-Related Careers

  • Civil Litigation
  • Criminal Litigation
  • Commercial and tribunal litigation and arbitration (NCLT, IBC, SAT, tax litigation, etc.)
  • Disputes and litigation team of a law firm
  • Litigation as a junior 
  • Litigation as an independent practitioner

 

Careers in a law firm/company

  • Corporate lawyer (in M&A, Banking & Finance, General Corporate, Capital Markets or another practice area) 
  • Employment lawyer
  • Intellectual property lawyer
  • Tax lawyer
  • Media and entertainment lawyer (in a media or IP law firm)
  • Technology lawyer
  • In-house counsel at an MNC or an Indian company

 

Preparation for judicial exams

  • Training for judgment writing - one of the most difficult skills tested in judicial exams
  • Course library covers courses for all state judicial exams and will help students in their early years in law college to kick start their preparation and get an early bird advantage
  • 2 hours of specialised classes per day round the year for judiciary training
  • You get access to a judiciary training course for 5 years or up to 2 years after your graduation, whichever is later even though access to other courses will terminate at the end of your law school

 

Career as a legal entrepreneur, independent practitioner or a founder of a law firm

  • Several law students are interested in starting their own firms after they graduate, often in a tier-2, tier 3 city or smaller town. They want to bring specialized expertise to clients who have a specific set of demands which are not addressed by the big city law firms in these far-flung regions. In such cases, with our support and training, students do not need to work for years in a Tier 1 corporate law firm to learn best practices, client and practice development-related skill sets, and can start off their law firm immediately after graduating.  
  • Additionally, if a law student intends to start his or her own venture (involving innovations around the use of the law, access to justice or even a venture unrelated to law), our courses will enable such a learner to address the legal, strategic, contractual and compliance aspects with ease. LawSikho also leverages its massive legal media assets to promote its alumni and their ventures.

 

Career as a freelance lawyer 

  • Many law students we speak to do not want to practice specifically as litigators, work in a law firm or in a company, or even build their own law firm. They want to consult clients independently and build a solo practise as freelancers. 
  • They may not live in a major commercial hub. They may build a practice while travelling the world. 
  • They may work on client assignments on a part-time or full-time basis, depending on their personal circumstances and career lifestyle preferences. 
  • These career options can be very fulfilling and sustainable, but the absence of practical skills currently prevents such lawyers from earning enough to live well and on their own. 
  • The lawyers who pursue this path are compelled to first find a job and work in a big law firm for years before they can build a career that suits their ambitions. However, having practical skills, knowledge of client acquisition and practice development can enable such lawyers to lay the groundwork for such a practice from law school days itself, and reap rich benefits from the day they graduate.

content_title: For Law Students/Law Graduates/Candidates Preparing For Competitive Exams (Law) / UPSC Aspirants/ Legal Practitioners/Individuals wishing to learn the Indian Constitution
content_details:
Knowing and Learning the Constitution of India is a gateway to attaining an upper hand towards all the other statutes of this Country. No wonder it is called the ‘Supreme Law or the Law of the Land.’

Just one benefit? Absolutely not! When it comes to the Constitution of India, no doubt the most exciting Legal subject, the advantages of gaining an upper hand are multifarious. To list a few: 
 

  • Knowledge of the Constitution, irrespective of the knowledge of any other discipline in law makes not only a law student, but also an individual empowered as regards the day to day affairs of the Nation  
  • Behind the stories and tales of the Indian Polity be it about the emergency period or the latest decision on the Ayodhya temple there are a plethora of exciting case laws that have shaped the interpretation of the Constitution of India. No wonder it is called a ‘’Living Document’ 
  • There is a trick behind reading and understanding the Bare Act and just like a treasure trove every reading of the Act will let you find something new. 
  • The Past Present and Future of the Constitution of this Nation is a once in a lifetime unforgettable journey that one must embark upon. 

Exciting as it sounds, students of the Constitution of India often seem to have a phobia regarding the learning of this Statute. Some of the doubts and myths that they attach  while going through this subject either while preparing for a competitive exam or otherwise are:

  • The Indian Constitution Act is bulky, never ending and a dull subject
  • Unfolding the concepts of this subject is unfeasible and an impossible task.
  • Case law based analysis of each concept makes it even more challenging.
  • There are innumerable case laws that one has to remember while understanding the Constitution. 
  • There is no logical sequence in which the Bare Act can be read, understood or remembered. 
  • Covering a few topics is sufficient while preparing for competitive exams. (Here one must note that tough competitive exams like UPSC and Judiciary often ask questions in Prelims and at times in Mains on Articles of the Bare Act which are otherwise not prominently covered in Law Colleges or otherwise covered in an ancillary manner.)  
  • It is difficult to keep a tap of and understand the holdings in the latest case laws when it comes to the Constitution of India.

content_title: All About LawSikho’s Crash Course Constitution
content_details:
It is easier to understand a detailed document rather than unfold the folds of a tiny act. The Indian Constitution Act is so profound in its nature that every reading of it will land you to learn a new concept. The minute details and cardinal principles of the Constitution of India should be known by anyone and everyone but due to its complicated and lengthy nature it becomes difficult to learn and understand the notions altogether, especially if not read in a logical manner.
 
The combination of both Constitutional and Administrative Law makes it convenient for students to gain a holistic knowledge of concepts which are more or less based on similar lines. For example, the doctrine of rule of law forms an integral part of Right to equality which is very well enshrined under Article 14 of the Indian Constitution.

Explore a teaching methodology that has made the subject interesting, interactive and completely antithetical to the idea of rote memorization. Learn something new with each content presentation on each topic

content_title: Are you attempting the SEBI Grade A Exam (for Legal Manager Position) this year?
content_details:
The SEBI Grade A Officers Position is a highly coveted job, with starting salaries INR 75,000 per month (with accommodation) or INR 1,07,000 per month (without accommodation) and a stable career path. 

There is however one caveat. 

The exam is highly competitive. 

Only 34 seats are available, of which 12 seats are for OBC, 8 for SC/ ST and 2 for EWB. Only a fraction of these seats (12) will be for lawyers. (For the Legal stream). [Please note that Lawyers are also eligible to appear for General Stream]

Even the most conservative estimates assume around 20,000 applicants to be sitting for this exam. 

In other words [20,000 sans the selected people] will be rejected.

This reflects a pass percentage of 0.2 percent at the maximum.

If you are preparing for the exam, definitely your intentions are that you don’t want to be in the rejected lot.

content_title: Top reasons why young lawyers fail to crack competitive exams
content_details:
• No way to track progress on a day-to-day, month-to-month basis.
  • No concrete clue of the syllabus or the areas where more focus should be laid upon. 
  • Lack of a strategy towards covering vast content in a lesser time.
  • Preparing for a competitive exam in the same way as a college exam because the syllabus overlaps.
  • Not identifying where they stand in comparison to others.
  • Not creating a sufficiently advanced preparation strategy for a national level competitive exam.
  • Absence of constant guidance.
  • Falling off their strategy.
  • Getting demotivated.
  • Insufficient practice on the exam format.
  • Believing that reading a book is sufficient to prepare for the exam.
  • Confused approach towards answering questions with knowledge gained by reading books.
  • Not measuring retention.
  • Not having a last-minute preparation strategy to revise.

content_title: Do you know the secrets that differentiate the few people who crack the exam from the thousands who don’t?
content_details:
• Measurement of where they stand
  • Guidance of experts
  • Continuous Optimisation of their strategy
  • Fixed path towards revision 
  • Attempts and Re-Attempts in practice until one gains perfection

content_title: How can you measure where you stand today, use it to improve your preparation, measure your progress, prepare again?
content_details:
• Measure topic-wise progress, till you master the subject
  • Measure subject-wise progress, till you master all the subjects
  • Measure syllabus-wise progress till you master time management strategy.
  • Measure overall-progress till you master the nuances of the entire syllabus.

content_title: Are you?
content_details:
Do you dream of becoming a judge after you graduate?
Are you attempting the judiciary exam anytime soon?
Struggling with preparation? Do you find it difficult to cover the vast syllabus?
Is time management and prioritisation proving to be a challenge? Do you want to figure out how to stay focussed and make consistent progress?
Are you facing difficulty in balancing preparation with law school life or alongside your practice or job? Do you want to figure out ways to study effectively without having to compromise on academics, your job or practice?

content_title: Belief-systems which frequently mislead first-timers who attempt the judiciary exams
content_details:
If I study hard over a period of time, I should clear the exam. If I still don’t, then it is out of my hands. After all, what else could I do? 

I will start preparation in full swing in my final year or after I graduate. 

I can sufficiently prepare for judiciary exams if I follow my college studies for the subjects which are covered in the LLB syllabus, at least till the 4th or 5th year. 

I am a class topper. Nobody can tell me better than what I can already accomplish on my own. I will prepare on my own. If I fail, we will see then.    

It is too early to start preparation now. I will first explore different career options, pursue different internships and then start preparing later. 

I can borrow notes from others who have enrolled in a coaching class and take help from my friends who go to the coaching class.

I will get guidance from my senior or relative who has cracked the exam. 

I will read books and Bare Acts - that is sufficient to crack the exam. 

Destiny and luck are the only major components to crack a competitive exam such as judiciary - there is no scientific way to prepare. 

Browsing through all the free content available on the internet/ YouTube will help be sufficient for my first attempt. 

Several subjects are common across multiple states. Preparing for one State’s Judiciary will automatically help me crack other State Judiciary Exams as well.

content_title: Journey of an average law student who wants to crack the judiciary exam
content_details:
First year: 

This is too early to start, of course. I have 2 more/ 4 more years (depending on whether you are in 3 years or 5 years course)
 

Second-year: 

Ok, now they are teaching some relevant subjects like IPC, CPC, CrPC, Evidence Act, so let me learn these from college teachers first, then I will join judiciary coaching later.
 

Third-year: 

Yeah, now I need to start thinking about judiciary preparation, but I guess I still have time. I will start next month. No, I will start after the next exam. Ok, after Diwali. Fine, after New Year definitely etc.
 

Fourth-year: 

I still have not started judiciary training. But I guess it’s ok. Maybe I should think of joining a judiciary coaching finally. 
 

Fifth-year: 

I have joined a judiciary coaching class finally. However, now I have only 18 months to prepare 40 huge subjects. It’s bigger than my entire law school curriculum to finish this in 18 months now, and I need to study for 12 hours a day! Ok, maybe I can do this. Let me try.
 

After 2 months: 

It’s not happening. How can one study for 10 hours a day? I am getting depressed from staying in front of books and not being able to focus! My life is upside down, and still, I am not progressing fast enough. Maybe I should try again after graduation when I can focus exclusively on this. Also, this is the final year in college, and I should enjoy this year and not spend studying for 10 hours a day!
 

3 months after graduation: 

All my friends are earning, dating, traveling, posting amazing pictures on Instagram, and what am I doing? Trying to learn CPC and TOPA notes, and I do not know where to start and where to end. Am I ready to study so much for the next 12-18 months? What if I don’t make it after all this effort?
 

What happens next

80% of judiciary-aspirants psychologically give up at this point. They may still appear in the exam, but they know in their heart that they have not put in the preparation that was needed. They still go through the motions to keep their family happy or to keep up appearances. But long before, they are already looking for exit options.

content_title: Can you relate to this pattern?
content_details:
This pattern is an outcome of the belief systems highlighted above. 

  • These belief systems create a false sense of security. Intelligent candidates end up procrastinating the real work of preparation. 
  • Instead of giving you more time, you get less time to effectively prepare, which increases the risk.

content_title: 5 steps to secure your judiciary preparation
content_details:
#1 - State-focussed preparation

Every state has a different judiciary exam format. Even in states where some of the subjects are common, the types of questions and weightage to those subjects differ widely. 

Therefore, preparation needs to be state-specific. Studying the subjects in your LLB syllabus or taking additional classrooms without focus on state-specific papers does not prepare you for the different state judiciary exams.  

Identify the exams you will attempt before you start preparing. 

A detailed trends analysis needs to be conducted for those states based on at least 10 years’ question papers.

You will then need to customise your preparation based on the types of questions and the weightage on them in the respective state judicial services exams. 

Also, leaving You will also need to develop a strategy for cracking.
 

#2 - Measurement-based approach at all times

You may have studied for 10 hours, but how many questions from that portion can you answer in the real exam? 

If you have read the books and bare acts, say in Code of Civil Procedure, but cannot answer questions on it in a mock, your preparation is incomplete.

Most candidates  deploy incorrect or suboptimal preparation techniques for years without ever finding out how to improve.

They study for months and years from books, bare acts, and notes but do not have any idea about where they stand with respect to the competition. 

What if there was a yardstick which assisted you towards assessing at which stage of your preparation you currently stand?

What if you followed this every day to track your progress and improve your effectiveness? 

A measurement-based approach is necessary. You will need to periodically iterate your strategy based on the measurements.
 

#3 - Appropriate focus on the ‘Mains’ exam

If you want to crack the mains, you need to prepare to write subjective answers from a very early stage in your preparation. Some of the mistaken beliefs that lead to failure in the mains exams are:   

  • I will refer to model answers - this does not improve your own writing skills. 
  • I will take up a legal writing course - this does not enable you to prepare and write better answers for judiciary exams.
  • I will prepare for mains after I first crack the prelims - if you manage to crack the prelims, this one belief will come in your way.
  • I am learning the answers every day - memorization does not enable you to reproduce during the exam, especially when questions are frequently changed.

 

College-answer writing skills do not equate to judiciary mains exams skills. 

To improve your ability to write answers, you need to practice real answer-writing every day and get corrections. Imagine doing that for a few years. Where will you stand in comparison to those who do this work last minute?
 

#4 - Target-based preparation customised to your abilities

Your strengths and weaknesses and your aptitude for grasping various subjects in the syllabus are vastly different from another candidate, whether it is your batchmate or someone who has been practising for a couple of years. 

Therefore, a personalised study plan which is target-based is very important. How is this done? Usually, such a plan is created after attempting a diagnostic test with the help of someone who has coached others to successfully crack the exam.
 

#5 - Selection of the right kind of coaching for guidance

The journey for the exam is long and tiring. Ideally, candidates need to study for 14-15 hours for 1.5 years at least merely to complete the syllabus. 

They need guidance, but all forms of guidance are not the same. 

For example, it will be very difficult to crack the judiciary exams through Board Exam coaching or school tuitions. Preparation to crack a competitive exam needs to be more specific. 

How to select coaching that fits your goals? 

  • Detailed trends analysis to save you time
  • Guidance on a personalised strategy and study plan
  • Frequent interventions to motivate 
  • Repository of materials to go through during self-study
  • Answer-writing feedback and corrections
  • Intensive classroom program 
  • Rich variety of tests to track your own daily and monthly progress and see where you stand with respect to the competition 

For those who want to first try it on their own before you take coaching, please read this page again. 

This is the most difficult exam that you have probably ever attempted, and there is no comparison with any college or other exam. 

For those of you who attempted the CLAT exam, it does not even come close to the kind of competition and difficulty that you will face in the judiciary exam. 

It is also unlikely that we have a track record for this kind of intensive self-preparation for 14-15 days. For most candidates, the maximum time that they have spent preparing is about 6-8 hours per day over a period of 10 days to a month.    

If college or CLAT exams were a sprint, this is an ultra-marathon, with more difficult competition and fewer seats.

Therefore, the real question is - when should you take guidance, what is the guidance that you need and how to select the right coaching class.

content_title: For Law Students/ Law Graduates/Candidates Preparing For Competitive Exams (Law) // Legal Practitioners/ Individuals wishing to learn the Criminal Procedure Code
content_details:
What are the First Questions that come to your mind when you think about studying the Code of Criminal Procedure?

  • How do I start reading the Bare Act?
  • In what sequence are the sections to be read?
  • What is to be read and what is to be left?
  • How am I supposed to navigate a subject which appears too technical?
  • Is CrPC relatively mechanical as compared to other subjects?
  • Do you feel ill-equipped when it comes to having a good theoretical hold on the Code of Criminal Procedure?

 

Beware of the common misconceptions about learning the Code of Criminal Procedure:

  • The Code of Criminal Procedure is to be covered in an isolated manner. 
  • You need to have a good hold on the Indian Penal Code and other substantive laws before starting this subject. 
  • There are only a couple of provisions which one must know, the rest can be left. 
  • There are no existing shortcuts to cover the important provisions in an effective manner. 
  • Rote learning is the single way to acquire a basic hold over the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 

Why is LawSikho launching a Crash Course on the Code of Criminal Procedure?

Any criminal system of a Country, not only needs recognition of wrongs and their punishments but also needs a procedure to make those mischieves punishable. As an extension of the abovementioned assertion, a powerful substantive law as the Indian Penal Code is redundant if there is no procedure to identify the violations therein and implement a process towards creating an effective deterrence. 

Let us understand this through an example, Section 498 of the Indian Penal Code defines and penalizes defamation and makes it a crime, but what needs to be done when defamation is committed is given under Section 199 of the Criminal Procedure Code. 

Often devoid of practical experience at a learning stage, students of law find it difficult to understand and learn this subject particularly for course curriculums and competitive exams. A conventional reading of the Bare Act, seldom serves any effective purpose. A thorough understanding of the subject entails categorizing the Bare Act into various parts as per the roles and functions defined, interlinking the various provisions within the Code as well as connecting the dots with various other criminal statutes as well as drawing a comparative analysis with the Code of Civil Procedure.

content_title: Walkthrough of LawSikho’s Criminal Procedure Law Crash Course
content_details:
As most of us would agree, Criminal law in our Country is indeed a very interesting discourse.. It is significant to understand the nitigrities of this branch of law by every lawyer. Criminal Procedure provides a detailed procedure for criminal laws to meet their ends. It is like a thread adjoining crime and justice. 

LawSikho is here with a complete guide for the same where uncoding the subject becomes an easy ride with an exhaustive set of notes on each topic along with interactive quizzes and pre-recorded sessions. 

Explore a teaching methodology that has made the subject interesting, interactive and completely antithetical to the idea of rote memorization. Learn something new with  content presentation on each topic.

What is exceptional about this Course? The live classes in this course would be taken by a faculty who is a top level expert when it comes to teaching the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Our star faculty Mr. Harshit Sharma is a Selected Candidate RJS 2018, AIR-68 DJS (2019), AIR 15 and 23 CLAT PG 2019 and 20, NET Qualified, Doctoral Candidate PhD at NLU Jodhpur. 

His varied experience at successfully qualifying some of the country’s toughest competitive exams  and a zeal to contribute towards the discourse will not only help the students in their preparation for the subject, but literally would turn out to be a strategy for each student’s success.

content_title: For Law Students/ Law Graduates/Candidates Preparing For Competitive Exams (Law) /Legal Practitioners/ Individuals wishing to learn the Indian Evidence Act.
content_details:
What are the First Questions that come to your mind when you think about studying the Indian Evidence Act?

  • Apart from Civil and Criminal law, why do I have to study the Indian Evidence Act?
  • What is the relevance of Evidence Law as a legal subject in theory and practice?
  • How to start reading the bare act and keep the important provisions in mind?
  • Is there a shortcut to get over it because of its compact size?
  • Do you think that the technical nature of the subject makes it a tough exercise to grasp all the concepts at one go?
  • How does one connect the dots of the Indian Evidence Act with other civil as well as criminal laws.

 

Beware of the common misconceptions about learning the Indian Evidence Act:

  • You have to get a grasp on the  Indian Penal Code and Criminal Procedure Code before learning the Indian Evidence Act.
  • This subject is altogether less important than other mainstreams law subjects and lesser number of provisions are always easy to cover.
  • The Indian Evidence Act need not be read in an interconnected manner with other civil and criminal legal aspects.
  • Only the first 55 sections which form the part of Relevance are important and the rest are of no significance. 
  • Visiting the Courtroom itself explains the principles of the subject, there is no need to refer to the bare act.
  • All the provisions of the Evidence Act is criminal in nature and they have no connection with the civil branch of law.
  • All the legislative Acts framed before the era of independence are well drafted and easy to uncode.

 

Why is LawSikho launching a Crash Course on the Indian Evidence Act?

The law of Evidence is that adjective law without which there can be no adjudication. It is an inseparable part of the structure of Criminal law specially which should not be just done away with. It not only governs the admissibility and relevancy of evidence but also determines those categories of evidence which can be taken into consideration in a court of law. 

A good lawyer/judiciary aspirant should not only be acquainted with those principles but also have them in his tip of fingers as this subject forms a decisive factor in deciding a case. A perfect example for this would be Section 32(1) which makes the evidence given by a person dying relevant on a presumption that a person cannot die with a lie in his mouth. 

This high is the practical importance of the subject both in competitive exams and academic spheres. A basic reading of 167 sections would not serve the ends but an exhaustive understanding of each and every concept in relation to other connected subjects like Indian Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Code is highly recommended.

content_title: Introduction
content_details:
I have a practice in the High Court and other forums. I feel like an outsider when
I go to the Supreme Court with a matter.

I think Supreme Court practice requires some superior degree of knowledge and
acumen and it is not my cup of tea.

I look forward to practicing in the Supreme Court someday. But I do not know how to do it.

I think I am t too young to start practicing in the Supreme Court

I am a law student and I want a launchpad and certainty to my career by starting to practice before the Supreme Court.

I have just started my practice and I want to fast track the time by building a supporting practice before the Supreme Court for matters arising in my state.

I practice in another city. I do not know how to start practicing in the Supreme Court

I want to step up and build my credibility as a top lawyer in my city and be able to argue state matters before the Supreme Court.

I want to fast track my career and move to Supreme Court from Trial Court and High Court practice and may come back with higher credibility.

I have clients who have matters in the Supreme Court. I do not know how to retain them.

I am getting a few matters in the Supreme Court, but how do I grow this work further?

What would it take for me to become an Advocate-on-Record? Do I have to go to Delhi and start figuring this out from scratch?

I do not read enough judgments to have the required knowledge to practice in the Supreme Court.

I want to take important constitutional matters and public causes of my city before the concerned High Court and Supreme Court and build my credibility.

If these questions come to your mind or resonate with you, you are at the right place.

We have solutions to all these questions. This is India’s one and only course where we train lawyers to develop a Supreme Court practice.

The best part about Supreme Court practice is that every bit of knowledge and experience you have gained in the trial court and/or the High Court or any other forum comes handy when you are handling matters in the Supreme Court.

You get to put to use all your strengths only if you know how and where to use them. 

Litigation in the Supreme Court has a place for everybody. 

Even if you do not regularly appear in the matters before the Supreme Court, just being a Supreme Court advocate gives you unparalleled exposure and credibility while arguing before the High Court.

There are lawyers who are good at getting the job done: they know whom to engage, when to engage, where to get the drafting done and they may earn more than many designated Senior Advocates. 

There are others who draft well. There are those who are good arguing counsels and are hired for putting the points together in a manner that nobody else can.

There are those who just act as advocate-on-record and play a very limited role.

There are some all-rounders. There are many outstation lawyers who do matters in the Supreme Court once in a while. The Supreme Court has space for all of them.

We have designed a course that gives you an opportunity to develop your own USP with the help of meticulously designed exercises so that you can find your space in this universe. 

Our course will provide you an insight into the Supreme Court practice and train you using a hands-on approach that emulates the training you would otherwise have to receive in a senior’s chamber by apprenticing for years. 

In this course we will hone your research, drafting, and arguing skills specifically for Supreme Court practice. Beside that, we will also guide you on how to deal with day-to-day practical challenges you will face, and how to grow your practice and profile. 

We will impart a holistic training so that you feel at ease while walking down the corridors of the Supreme Court. 

We will ensure that you are equipped with enough skills to both brief any Senior Advocate if your matter reaches the Supreme Court.

We will also go into detail of constitutional matters before the High Court including Writ Petitions and Public Interest Litigations to help you build your credibility in the state High Court and have leading matters before the Supreme Court.

Those appearing for the Advocate-on-Record examination in June 2021 and 2022  can also apply and benefit from this course.

content_details:

  • How Registry functions
  • Comparative knowledge of the applicability of various jurisdictions
  • Different methods of quick and effective research required for Supreme Court litigation
  • Sound knowledge of what works and what does not

  • Standards & parameters to draft persuasive petitions/appeals
  • Drafting and arguing skills and court craft
  • Strategizing and preparing for arguments

  • How to go about developing a Supreme Court practice

content_title: Who should take this course?
content_details:
• Lawyers who want to start their Supreme Court practice from home state, or move to Delhi.
  • Lawyers who want to foray into the Supreme Court Practice along with their trial and High Court practice.
  • Independent practitioners who want to brief lawyers in Supreme Court matters.
  • Lawyers who want to crack the Advocate-on-Record exam and build a practice in Supreme Court
  • Lawyers who want to argue before the Supreme Court as arguing counsel.
  • Lawyers or law students who are aiming to work as junior to well-known senior advocates.
  • Law students who want to kickstart their practice by starting from the Supreme Court right away after their law school.
  • Law students who want to intern in chambers of Advocate-on-Record and develop early exposure to Supreme Court work
  • In-house counsels of big companies (which frequently litigate in the Supreme Court)
  • Lawyers in disputes teams of law firms if they have to take up Supreme Court matters

content_title: What career options will open up for you after this course?
content_details:
• Whether you have an independent practice in any part of India or you are working as a lawyer in the disputes team of a law firm, learning Supreme Court work will be useful for you when it comes to the most important cases of your life.
  • You’ll be trained in a manner that you can develop a full-fledged Supreme Court practice. You may be a fresher, working at a law firm, in-house counsel, or practicing in the High Court of any State, district courts, or any other forum, it’s never too late nor too early to move your practice to the Supreme Court. Everyone has some opportunity though the scope may vary.
  • You’ll be able to advise clients on when and how they can approach the Supreme Court. Thus, you won’t lose your client when they want to file an appeal or an SLP before the Supreme Court or when the other party does it. 
  • Think of your best and largest clients - you may be handling their matters regularly. You already have an edge over other counsels. You know the matter inside out and the client trusts you at least to the extent that you know the matter. They would be more comfortable with you than with any other lawyer. Therefore, there’s no reason why you should let this opportunity go by referring them to a ‘Supreme Court lawyer’. That’s because there’s no such thing as a ‘Supreme Court lawyer’. Either there are Advocate-on-record or there are Senior Advocates. Rest of them are just advocates handling Supreme Court matters and you can be one of them. This course will help to bridge the gap and equip you to handle Supreme Court matters all by yourself.
  • Supreme Court practice is one of its kind that gives you an opportunity to do what you know the best and delegate the rest of the work if you want. An Advocate-on-record can be engaged only for the purpose of filing a petition while the counsel handling the matter below may take care of the rest. If you are an Advocate-on-record, you get to charge 15K just for filing. This course equips you to handle all aspects of drafting, filing and arguing matters in the Supreme Court. 
  • Many lawyers start practicing in the Supreme Court straight after college as a junior to an Advocate-on-record or Senior Advocate. But they don’t have exposure on trial court work. The focus is just on getting the work done on time. They don’t get time to learn, and develop the skills required to do their work more effectively. Compared to these lawyers, you will be in a far superior position after doing this course.
  • There are lawyers with a practice in a different forum and have some exposure on handling Supreme Court matters. But they do not get to attend and observe the proceedings of the Supreme Court regularly to know what works and what does not. This course helps to bridge the gap for both sets of lawyers by working on all the skills required for a successful practice in the Supreme Court. 
  • By the end of the course, you’ll be able to strategize, identify grounds and prepare an effective draft without the need to hire anyone else for drafting. You can also brief senior counsels effectively. The advantage of a practice with different lawyers playing different roles is that you can charge well for the part of the job you do the best. This course helps you identify what you do best and further strengthen it.
  • You’ll be conversant with drafting Supreme Court petitions effectively. It means that if you are an in-house counsel, you’ll be able to review drafts prepared by Advocate-on-record for your client/ company effectively and can easily impress people with your knowledge of how things work in the Supreme Court.
  • This course will also train you to crack the Advocate-on-Record examination by exhaustively covering all the four papers: Practice & Procedure, Drafting, Advocacy & Professional Ethics and Leading Cases. 
  • We’ll also have practice sessions and you’ll get feedback on your answers to question papers of the previous years. Those appearing for the Advocate-on-record examination in June 2021 and 2022  will find it fruitful because they get to complete their entire preparation before the examination.
  • You’ll be equipped to handle the filing at the Registry and matters before the Registrar’s court. While many lawyers practising in the Supreme Court for years themselves do not know how matters are filed, it is a basic requirement for an Advocate-on-Record, something that everyone expects you to know the moment you become an Advocate-on-Record. So you’ll not just be prepared to take the Advocate-on-Record examination, you also get trained in doing your job even before becoming an Advocate-on-Record.

content_title: Specific Learning Objectives
content_details:
How to read and analyze an impugned order

  • Learn to skim through an Impugned Order marking the territory of facts, evidence in criminal matters, submissions and findings.
  • Learn to scan through an Impugned Order with the objective of identifying grounds, looking for how the High Court erred or failed to consider legally relevant aspects.
  • Learn to identify and distinguish questions of law from questions of facts.
  • Learn to identify the research points quickly and to ensure it is exhaustive in nature.
  • Explore different kinds of research tools and define your approach to research so that each time you are confronted with a legal problem, you simply follow those steps to find answers. 
  • Understand the factors that determine how you approach a legal issue and where you begin your research.
  • Devise methods to ensure that your research is exhaustive and you achieve the highest quality of research in every case you work on.
  • Learn and practice dealing with upsets and dead ends successfully during research.
  • Learn to identify relevant key-words and legal propositions while researching on different online/offline legal databases.

What to cite? How much to cite?

  • Learn to skim and scan through judgments and quickly find what you need.
  • Learn to examine the relevance of a judgment, whether wholly or in parts, connecting with or distinguishing from the facts of the present case.
  • Develop an understanding of the various stages of litigation leading to the passing of the Impugned Order / Judgement.
  • Learn to cull out the 'settled law' relating to an issue and express it effectively in a petition or before a judge so that even when you paraphrase what you have read, the meaning is not lost 
  • Learn to use/refer a part of a judgment in the pleadings in a manner that would have the maximum impact, know which part of a judgment to quote, decide on whether to quote or not
  • Learn to understand contextual interpretations of judgments delivered by the Supreme Court to avoid using judgments out of context.
  • Learn to differentiate between ratio decidendi and obiter dicta while reading a judgement and cite settled position of law accordingly.

Devising different strategies for different kinds of petitions

  • Learn to draft various petitions, appeals, suit and applications filed before the Supreme Court using hands-on approach 
  • Hone drafting skills keeping in mind the following aspects:
    • Maintainability
    • Making the ingredients evident in the course of narrating the facts and stating the grounds
    • Understanding what would constitute material facts for a petition or appeal before the Supreme Court
    • Appreciating the possibility of experimenting with ideas and language

What to plead? How to plead?

  • Devising strategies and preparing a set of grounds that work and those that can be made to work
  • How to plead facts and circumstances
  • Understand the facts and circumstances under which cases get decided in favour so that you may remember to plead them when they apply to you
  • Learn to use precise and accurate words with crisp language having legal significance, as used in authoritative texts.
  • Develop an understanding of the nature of fundamental rights while drafting the writ petition.
  • Understand how to bring out the violation of the fundamental right(s) in a manner and/or mould the relief sought to bring the case within the purview of Article 32 without the requirement of exhausting alternate remedy under Article 226.

How to prepare for hearings

  • Is the way we argue before the Supreme Court any different from other courts? Questions of law vis-a-vis questions of fact
  • Learn how to brief a Senior Advocate. We’ll do lots of roleplay simulation exercises
  • Learn to prepare notes for a Senior Advocate or for the purpose of briefing and arguing cases
  • Learn to differentiate the requirements and prepare for arguments keeping in mind the stage (notice/post-notice/final disposal) and nature (miscellaneous/regular) of hearing
  • Understand the factors that determine the content of oral arguments and how much to emphasise on a point. How do you decide at different stages? Again, we’ll do enough simulation exercises for you to get it
  • Understand when to stop and why and how to come back to a point at a later stage, if need be 
  • Learn to use storytelling as a skill during arguments

Written Submissions

  • Understand the purpose of filing Written Submissions/Convenience Note/Volume before the Supreme Court. When to file it
  • Learn how to structure your Written Submissions and differentiate it from the structure of the petition
  • Learn the usage of brief and concise language without losing persuasiveness and differentiate it with the language used in drafting the grounds of the petition
  • Find out the blunders people make while drafting Written Submissions and learn how to avoid them

Issuance of notice by Supreme Court: is it sheer luck?

  • An SLP may get dismissed and the file thrown away even before you get to blink your eye. Understanding the factors/hurdles/challenges involved in the issuance of notice by the Supreme Court and learn how to face them while drafting a petition to ensure notice is issued.
  • Understanding the thin line between a good draft and a not-so-good draft from the context of getting notice issued.
  • Learning how to present your case at the notice stage keeping the challenges in mind and differentiating it from the post-notice stage arguments. We’ll do roleplay simulation exercises.
  • How different is it to get a notice issued by the Supreme Court than in any other High Court

content_title: Introduction
content_details:
There are some very promising areas of law that lawyers do not take full advantage of. Labour and employment law is one of them. Combined with industrial laws it makes a very powerful combination. There are amazing opportunities both in terms of working as in-house lawyers, joining labour and employment team of law firms as well as build your own practice or consultancy as a labour and industrial law advisor and litigator.

Labour law was one of the subjects that really intrigued me when I was in law school. There so many new issues around labour and employment law, but why do they teach us a bunch of mostly irrelevant and extremely outdated things in name of labour law in law school? Sure, we need to know the basic concepts, and they taught that in law school, but highly important and relevant issues of our times were left out.

I was going through a few syllabuses of some of the top law schools last year. Things have not changed.

The result is that labour law has a pretty bad image with budding (and even most of the grown up) lawyers. It is often considered right next to CPC in being boring and maybe just above human rights law in terms of low potential for making money. At least that’s the perception that most lawyers and law students have.

I will tell you my experience. We began to offer a labour law course in 2016. It became popular quickly with HR managers, IR professionals, company secretaries and other compliance professionals. The percentage of lawyers who take the course is under 20%. All other law courses boasts of at least 50% of candidates from legal background.

However, it is a myth that labour law is boring or that you can’t make money as a labour lawyer. There is a huge amount of labour law work that is up for grabs, for several reason, and the biggest reason an upcoming lawyer should consider becoming an expert of labour laws is that there is very low competition for it. Let the rest of the world think that labour law is not sexy and miss out the opportunities, if you are looking for a break and willing to go for a relatively uncommon area of law, keep reading.

And of course, I need not tell HR managers or IR professionals about how valuable labour and employment law, coupled with industrial law, can be for their career. The subject is taught in MBA courses, but very poorly.

If you want thorough practical knowledge of labour laws as well as industrial laws, we have a course for you. However, before that, it is very important to understand a few important dynamics about labour law to fully recognize where the career opportunities are arising.

content_title: Labour law is changing
content_details:
One of the biggest complaint of India Inc has been that labour laws are complex in India. On the other hand, a large part of the Indians employed in jobs do not have protections of labour law as it is old and focuses on the manufacturing sector more and leaves out the service sector, which employ a large number of people. That is slowly but decisively changing.

The current government has an agenda of simplifying the labour laws. While no sweeping reforms has been made, some of the recent amendments have changed the nature of the game.

Take the Payment of Wages Act, for instance. The ceiling of salary, with respect to which employees it apply to, has been raised recently to INR 24,000, bringing a large number of employees under its umbrella and companies for whom it has suddenly become very relevant.

Similarly, a very interesting situation has presented itself after the recent amendments of the Maternity Benefits Act as women how have to be given 6 months of paid holiday when they get pregnant while they are employed. Given that churn of employees leaving is high in the private sector, and employees often leave within 1 or 2 years of joining a job, it has very cumbersome for employers who don’t expect employees to stay beyond a year or two, to hire married women. Legal claims of maternity benefits being denied as well as companies looking to defend themselves against such claims is suddenly on the rise.

For a long time, labour law was not a very viable career unless you wanted to work for factories and labourers. That is not the case any more. With every amendment and reforms, now you can expect more and more labour law/employment disputes involving white collar employees, where stakes are higher and volume is unprecedented.

And what is unfortunate, is that there are very few lawyers in the market to tap into these opportunities with any credible skills or knowledge of labour law.

content_title: Introduction
content_details:
Are you in the top management of a multinational company and want to develop an understanding of how international transactions are regulated?

Are you a business leader looking to lead your company into a newer market?

Are you interested in building a career in international business laws?

Do you want to be in high demand as a lawyer in industries and companies that are looking to expand their global presence? 

Do you want to get a credible international certification and exposure on your resume but find courses from top universities too expensive?

Are you preparing for an LLM in International Business Law from a foreign university?

Do you want to network with top US faculties, lawyers, and global experts that can open new opportunities for you?

Do you want a job in India or abroad as an in-house counsel with companies that have a multinational presence? 

Do you want to learn everything from drafting key transactional documents to international taxation and international commercial arbitration, necessary for a transaction lawyer advising clients across jurisdictions?

Are you a law student looking to secure recognition from an international university and eventually work abroad?

Do you want to strengthen your CV with a certificate from a university with significant global presence?

Are you interested in standing out due to your solid knowledge and skills around International Business Laws in every internship and interview?

If the answer to any of these questions is yes, read on.

When a lawyer and an entrepreneur negotiate, it is often said that one speaks Greek and other Latin. What seems to make business sense is often not aligned to what makes legal sense. A good business leader will often need to be able to make sense of both of these to ensure that the success script of their business is well written. 

The need for this ability to understand the legal side aggravates when you are looking to operate in multiple countries. You cannot be taking any chances when it comes to understanding the regulatory requirements of an economy you wish to expand to.

A founder looking to expand into another country cannot afford to blindly rely on external consultants to advise on the entry and continuing business operations in that country. Founders need awareness and an ability to choose the best from among the various options that may be presented by such consultants.

In fact, post-covid, most emerging economies are competing to attract foreign investment, luring businesses in global expansion. In line with this, many businesses are also looking to break barriers and expand beyond their country borders, to benefit from the opportunities, which makes this awareness essential for the founders.

Founders who are ably supported by in-house lawyers and consultants adept at market entry requirements and strategies have a clear advantage - they are unlikely to miss out on business opportunities which are of course, time sensitive.

With this impetus on entering new markets, it is natural that demand for business leaders and lawyers who have a keen understanding of international business law, regulatory environment and intricacies has seen a huge surge. 

As a business leader or a lawyer supporting such businesses, such an understanding not only gives a competitive edge, but also helps in mitigating key risks. The regulatory environment including taxation, ownership of property, ease of incorporation and liquidation play a key role in shaping these policies.

In fact, companies have increasingly started giving strong leadership positions to their general counsels who can play a key role, in negotiating cross border deals and finalising global strategies.

Some very essential questions that a business looking to enter into a new market and operate internationally would need to consider are:

  • What are the different modes of entry into the market and how to set up entities in that market?
  • What are the legislations governing foreign investment, taxation, labour and intellectual property in that market?
  • How would the cross border business transactions and contracts pan out?
  • What are the dispute resolution mechanisms available, including litigation?

It is very difficult to find knowledge bases or training to skill business leaders, lawyers and other professionals in answering even all of such elementary questions at one place. Most resources tend to focus on one or two aspects such as the legal systems of different countries and international taxation. 

We saw a necessity to build a programme which can provide such training in a very comprehensive manner, eliminating the need to search for different resources to meet such skill requirements. 

This course aims in combining all the key learnings that a business leader, an in-house counsels, a transactional lawyer or a management consultant would require to service their clients who are bound for crossing national borders.

Why did we launch this course?

We receive a lot of requests from business professionals, entrepreneurs,  lawyers, law students and management consultants looking for a clear understanding of how international business transactions work and factors significantly impacting such transactions such as taxation and dispute resolution mechanisms.

They want to be able to sit on the board and help their companies in identifying the right global strategy, taking into account various practical considerations.

For many of them, the only recourse is an expensive LLM or Master in Business Laws abroad or alternatively, a Masters in Business Administration program, post which there is no assurance that they will be able to secure any employment or clients enabling them to work on international projects or assignments.

We also wanted to do something that increases access of Indian business leaders and  lawyers to superb teaching and insights from experts across the world at a far lower cost compared to similar programs across the world.

This is what drew us to collaborating with Webster University a university with strong international presence, maintaining campuses in a multitude of countries across Europe and Asia and an extensive study-abroad program. The University boasts of a stunning 98% comprehensive job placement rate, among the best in its category.

content_title: About Webster University
content_details:
Webster University is a private university with its main campus in Webster Groves, Missouri. It is an independent, non-profit, non-denominational university with multiple branch locations across the United States. 

The university also has a strong international presence, maintaining campuses in a multitude of countries across Europe and Asia and an extensive study-abroad program. The University boasts of a stunning 98% comprehensive job placement rate, among the best in its category.

The university has an alumni network of around 170,000 graduates worldwide. It has proudly produced a number of celebrated people. It maintains a good alumni network with graduates serving global organizations. Some of the most famous alumni of the university include  Ann Wals Bradley, Wisconsin State Supreme Court Justice; John Boccieri, former US Congressman, William Broad, Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter for The New York Times, etc. 

We have designed this program carefully to service the needs of business leaders, law students, lawyers and management professionals. The program has comprehensive coverage, covering an introduction to various legal systems, understanding how contracts work, international taxation, essential insights on different regions and available dispute resolution mechanisms.

  • Entrepreneurs, business leaders and management consultants who want to understand the regulatory challenges in entering new markets.
  • In-house counsels, lawyers and other professionals working in companies with multinational presence;

content_title: What are the key skills that you will develop in this course?
content_details:
• The ability to understand the legal systems & basic principles of international law and dispute resolution mechanisms. 
  • The ability to understand the governing considerations while navigating into foreign markets with an insight into major economies of the world.
  • The ability to create tax strategies for global clients. This will be done through thinking from a ‘structuring’ perspective by understanding the functioning of tax havens and tax structures used by major corporations.
  • The ability to identify and strategize the best method of entry into newer markets and make comparative assessment of various regulatory considerations.
  • The ability to negotiate, understand, review and draft contracts effectively by understanding the major operative clauses that ensure maximum enforceability as well as risk mitigation clauses. 
  • The ability to engage in negotiations and dealing with mediation and arbitration involving international commercial disputes, right from understanding the applicable law to knowing how these processes work.
  • The ability to manage and negotiate international conflicts between commercial organisations and the role that lawyers play in the conflict management process.

content_title: What are the specific learning objectives of this course?
content_details:
• To understand legal systems around the world;
  • To understand basic principles of international law and how international contracts work;
  • To understand what kind of commercial dispute resolution mechanisms are available around the world;
  • To understand what kind of disputes can arise in cross border contracts and how alternative dispute resolution mechanisms can be used to deal with them;
  • To understand what can be a right time for a business to expand into a foreign market;
  • To understand factors determining the decisions on whether or not to enter into a foreign market;
  • To decide the right mode of entering a foreign market;
  • To understand different roadblocks that you are likely to face while entering a foreign market;
  • To gain an understanding of economic factors such sectors receiving maximum foreign investment and legal considerations such as laws relating to foreign investment, taxation, labour, intellectual property, real estate etc. in ten major economies i.e. China, United States of America, Middle East, United Kingdom, EU (Netherlands), Russia, Canada, Japan and Brazil;
  • To learn what is conflict management and the difference between conflict resolution and conflict management;
  • To understand the connection between diversity and conflict management;
  • To learn the role that lawyers can play in the conflict management process and in mediation for conflicts;
  • To understand the relevance of developing conflict management strategies at an individual level;
  • To gain an understanding of the technical and commercial aspects involved in advanced contract-specific negotiations;
  • To learn the art of drafting contractual clauses to achieve the intended objectives and avoid ambiguous clauses and uncertain interpretations;
  • To learn reviewing contracts with an objective of minimizing future disputes;
  • To develop the required negotiation skills before walking into a high-value contract negotiation;
  • To learn how to quickly grasp the most important business aspects that dictate terms of any given contract;
  • To learn to perform a risk analysis of any contract;
  • To get trained in understanding your client’s expectations, commercial objectives and ensuring that your draft reflects the concerns of your clients;
  • To learn avoiding mistakes that even seasoned lawyers end up making in the process of contract drafting and negotiation;
  • To learn skills for representing big corporations in contract negotiation and how it is different from working with smaller businesses and individuals;
  • To learn to identify when your business operations are subject to international tax laws;
  • To understand the basic models on which Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) are executed;
  • To learn how to find and read a DTAA and key tax categories in a DTAA;
  • To learn how to identify the kinds of information that can and cannot be shared as per tax information exchange provisions under DTAAs;
  • To gain an understanding of the popular international tax structures used by global businesses;
  • To learn how to take benefit of Safe Harbour Rules prevalent in India;
  • Learn about Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP) and Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) prevalent between different countries;
  • To learn how to initiate international commercial arbitration proceedings globally;
  • To learn how to browse through and interpret the arbitration law of foregin jurisdictions (relevant for offshore international arbitration;
  • To learn how to advise clients on selecting an appropriate seat and to initiate proceedings before courts of a foreign supervisory jurisdiction;
  • To identify when and how to use an expedited or fast track procedure of an international arbitration institution;
